title: Half-Noise Norm Bound by Randomization
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces whose coordinate atom weights are strictly positive and sum to $1$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product outcome space, and let $q\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $q\ge1$. Then the $q$-moment norm of the product noise operator at parameter $1/2$ applied to $f$ is at most the randomization moment norm of $f$: $\|T_{1/2}f\|_{q,P}\le\|Rf\|_q$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces
Every coordinate atom weight is strictly positive
The weights in each coordinate space sum to $1$
$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $q\ge1$. Then $\|T_{1/2}f\|_{q,P}\le(\mathbb E_{x\sim P}\mathbb E_r|\sum_S\chi_S(r)f_S(x)|^q)^{1/q}$, where $r$ is uniform on the Boolean cube. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
